title: Google Workspace MCP Goes GA, REST APIs Sunset Feb 2027

body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Google Workspace MCP servers and CLI officially launched November 24, 2026, with free Standard tier covering over 99% of active developers.
- AI agents must migrate from traditional REST APIs to MCP by February 1, 2027, when REST access will be discontinued for Workspace services.
- New Scaled tier billing starts April 1, 2027, with expanded enterprise controls including per-agent data policies and admin oversight dashboards.


Google officially launched its Workspace[Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers](https://emergent.sh/glossary/what-is-mcp-server) and Workspace CLI on November 24, 2026, marking a fundamental shift in how AI agents access Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Chat, and Tasks. The company set a hard February 1, 2027 deadline for developers to migrate AI agents from traditional[REST APIs](https://emergent.sh/glossary/rest-api) to MCP, stating that REST infrastructure is designed for deterministic application calls while MCP is purpose-built for dynamic agent workflows.


The release includes two standardized usage tiers: a free Standard tier that covers more than 99% of active developers, and a paid Scaled tier with higher quotas that begins billing on April 1, 2027. Google emphasized that the same privacy, data loss prevention (DLP), and data protection standards apply across both tiers.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on November 24, 2026, the Workspace MCP servers and CLI are now generally available to all developers. The Standard tier provides immediate access at no cost, while the Scaled tier will begin charging on April 1, 2027. Organizations have until February 1, 2027 to complete their migration from REST APIs to MCP-based integrations.


Google Cloud Support customers will see Workspace APIs excluded from the support variable fee calculation until at least December 2027, with any changes communicated at least 90 days in advance. The initial general availability covers Gmail, Drive, and Calendar, with additional data access mechanisms scheduled for similar updates in the coming months.


## Why Google Is Deprecating REST APIs for Agents


Google distinguished between traditional REST APIs and MCP by highlighting architectural differences in how they handle agent workflows. REST APIs were built for predictable, synchronous application calls where the developer controls the exact sequence of operations. MCP, by contrast, is designed for autonomous agents that make dynamic decisions about which data to access and when.


The MCP servers provide unified authentication, automatic retry logic, and context-aware data access that agents need to operate reliably across Workspace services. By consolidating agent access through MCP, Google can apply consistent governance policies, monitor agent behavior in real time, and give administrators granular control over what data each agent can access. The company stated that maintaining parallel REST and MCP infrastructure for agent use cases would create security and reliability risks as agent adoption scales.


## Standardized Usage Tiers and Billing


The new tier structure aims to simplify quota management for developers building at scale. The Standard tier offers sufficient quota for over 99% of current active developers and remains free indefinitely. Developers who exceed Standard tier limits can opt into the Scaled tier, which provides higher quotas and begins billing on April 1, 2027.


Google did not disclose specific pricing details for the Scaled tier but confirmed that the same data protection standards apply across both tiers. The tiered model applies initially to Gmail, Drive, and Calendar APIs, with additional Workspace services transitioning to the same structure in coming months. Developers can monitor their usage through the Google Cloud Console to determine whether they need to upgrade before the April billing date.


## Enterprise Controls and Data Governance


Alongside the MCP general availability, Google introduced a new Workspace AI Tools Addendum and expanded enterprise controls for organizations managing AI agent access. Administrators can now set per-agent data access policies, view which agents have accessed Workspace data in audit logs, and revoke agent permissions from a centralized dashboard.


The company committed to rolling out more granular agent policies and controls over the coming months, including the ability to restrict agent access by organizational unit, data classification label, and user role. These controls extend the same governance principles that Workspace customers currently use for traditional applications, ensuring that agents operate within defined security boundaries even as they autonomously navigate data.


## What This Means


Google's MCP general availability represents a strategic bet that AI agents will become the primary interface for knowledge work, requiring infrastructure optimized for autonomous decision-making rather than deterministic API calls. The February 2027 REST sunset deadline forces developers to adopt MCP or lose Workspace integration, accelerating the platform shift. For enterprises, the new governance controls address a critical gap: how to maintain data oversight when agents, not humans, are making access decisions. Organizations now have three months to audit their current Workspace integrations, identify which agents rely on REST APIs, and complete the migration to MCP before the cutoff.
